title: Minimum-n rules and derived values (for example the hype gap)
description:
As a reader, I want values shown only when there is enough data, so that I am not misled by two votes.

Rules (configurable per publication, defaults shown): a dimension mean is shown with "n=3, too few" when n < 5; derived values (for example the gap between the mean of two "buzz" dimensions and the mean of two "substance" dimensions) show an em dash when any input has n < 5; ranking requires a floor of votes or the item appears under "New". Derived values are computed in the snapshot job, not in the browser.

```gherkin
Feature: Minimum-n rules
  Scenario: Too few ratings
    Given a dimension with 3 ratings and a floor of 5
    Then the mean is flagged too few and the derived value is a dash

  Scenario: Enough ratings
    Given all inputs have at least 5 ratings
    Then the derived value is computed and its sign is shown

  Scenario: Partially rated item
    Given an item rated on 2 of 4 dimensions
    Then it displays the rated dimensions and is not ranked by a composite
```

comments.text: Reconciliation 2026-10-22. Partly done. Exists: snapshot.hypeMinimum (default 5): the hype gap is null unless every dimension has enough reader ratings, computed in the snapshot job, not the browser (#516); the hype gap computed from config groups, readers and editors separately (#521); ranking.readerMinimum floor before the reader composite counts in Front (#516, ranking.py); partially rated items are not ranked by a composite. Remains: the 'too few' flag on a dimension mean in the components, the em dash display for a null derived value, and a 'New' queue for items below the ranking floor.
